_comment: Deep-strike triage citations (SWEG_DEEP_STRIKE_TRIAGE, default-on). BSData v10.6.0 attaches the standard Core Rules 'Deep Strike' ability directly to certain fast Aeldari/Drukhari skimmer, transport and gunship datasheets. Deep Strike is ALWAYS an optional player choice (the core rule reads 'you can set it up in Reserves instead of on the battlefield' — never mandatory). In 10th-edition competitive play these units are deployed on-board from Turn 1 because their value is Turn-1 board presence, but the simulator's faction-blind deploy AI (SWEG_DEPLOY_AI, simulator.py ~7404) routes every deep_strike=True unit into strategic reserves on Turn 1, breaking their doctrine — the same faction-blind reserve-split bug flagged in docs/DECISION_LEDGER.md (the deploy AI over-reserves deep-strike-capable units regardless of whether reserving is the competitively-correct choice). This gate corrects the DEPLOYMENT CHOICE for a confirmed list of these units by clearing deep_strike=False so the deploy AI keeps them on-board; it is a per-unit deployment-piloting correction, NOT a claim that the units lack the ability (they do have the real, optional Core Rules Deep Strike). Units that genuinely and routinely deep strike (Terminators, Crisis Battlesuits, Daemon units, Drop Pods, Nemesis Dreadknights, etc.) are NOT in the clear list. IMPORTANT CORRECTION (verified against local cache data/bsdata/cache/Aeldari - Aeldari Library.cat.gz): an earlier draft of these citations invented ability names ('Webway Portal', 'Webway Assault', 'Webway Gate') that do NOT appear on any of these datasheets (0 occurrences in the Aeldari Library); the actual and only mechanism is the standard unconditional Core Rules Deep Strike, quoted below.

loader.deep_strike_triage.deploy_pilotin.rule_name: Deep Strike (10e Core Rules) — an optional deployment choice, applied as a per-unit deployment-piloting correction
loader.deep_strike_triage.deploy_pilotin.quoted_text: During the Declare Battle Formations step, if all of the models in a unit have the Deep Strike ability, you can set that unit up in Reserves instead of setting it up on the battlefield. In the Reinforcements step of one of your Movement phases you can set up this unit anywhere on the battlefield that is more than 9" horizontally away from all enemy models.
loader.deep_strike_triage.deploy_pilotin.trigger: SWEG_DEEP_STRIKE_TRIAGE=1 (default); fires in code.bsdata.loader._apply_override for any unit key in _DEEP_STRIKE_TRIAGE_CLEAR_KEYS, overriding deep_strike to False. When the gate is OFF (SWEG_DEEP_STRIKE_TRIAGE=0) the BSData-verbatim flag is restored and the parse is byte-identical to the pre-triage code.
loader.deep_strike_triage.deploy_pilotin.effect: Clears deep_strike=True to False for the confirmed list of fast Aeldari/Drukhari skimmers, transports and gunships. The faction-blind SWEG_DEPLOY_AI then keeps these units on-board rather than routing them to strategic reserves on Turn 1, matching competitive play. This is a deployment-piloting correction expressed through the deep_strike flag (the flag is the only input the deploy AI reads); the units retain their real, optional Core Rules Deep Strike ability in the datasheet sense. NOT a rules claim that they cannot deep strike. The more faithful long-term fix is to make the deploy AI itself choose on-board deployment for these units (keeping deep_strike=True) — see docs/DECISION_LEDGER.md on the faction-blind reserve split; this per-unit gate is the scoped, only-improves interim that avoids a global deploy-AI change (which would also deploy over-pole factions such as Emperor's Children on-board, wrong-direction for the metric).
loader.deep_strike_triage.deploy_pilotin.note: BSData verification (data/bsdata/cache/Aeldari - Aeldari Library.cat.gz): every cleared unit carries 'Deep Strike' as a DIRECT, UNCONDITIONAL infoLink on its unit entry (not nested in a wargear/upgrade subtree, and with no modifier or condition). The mandatory/default deep-strike use case only applies to units with no other legal deployment (Drop Pods); for these fast transports it is an optional tool competitive play does not use, so on-board deployment is the faithful default. BSData reference: Warhammer 40,000 core rules, Deep Strike (BSData Warhammer 40,000.gst rule id 7cb5-dd6b-dd87-ad3b; cross-reference https://wahapedia.ru/wh40k10ed/the-rules/core-rules/#Reinforcements)

Passengers embarked pre-game ride with the Raider instead of being co-routed to reserves.
loader.deep_strike_triage.drukhari_raide.note: Confirmed dominant misplay in data/_drukhari_strategy_investigation.md: with deep_strike=True, all three Raiders in the Skysplinter Assault archetype plus their pre-embarked passengers are parked in reserves Turn 1, cancelling the entire alpha-strike. Deep Strike is a real but optional ability on the Raider; the competitive default is on-board deployment. BSData reference: data/bsdata/cache/Aeldari - Aeldari Library.cat.gz (Raider selectionEntry, direct unconditional 'Deep Strike' infoLink); data/_drukhari_strategy_investigation.md
